name: SanDisk Corporation
window: Q3 FY26 print + intra-quarter · Apr 30 → Jul 28, 2026

events.text: Q3 FY26 (quarter ended Apr 3, 2026): revenue $5.95B (+97% QoQ, +251% YoY), well above the $4.4-4.8B guide; non-GAAP GM 78.4% (vs 51.1%; guide 65-67%); non-GAAP EPS $23.41. Bits flat YoY and -high-teens QoQ — the move is all price/mix. Data center $1.467B (+233% QoQ). Five NBMs signed, $42B of minimum contractual revenue, >$11B of guarantees, covering >1/3 of FY27 bits. Q4 guide: rev $7.75-8.25B, GM 79-81%, EPS $30-33; $6B buyback authorized.

events.src: Bernstein · expert ex-WDC NAND VP Rob (HDD/NAND)
events.text: Mechanics of NBM enforceability: ~$11B of guarantees on ~$42B (~25%) — in a severe downturn, a customer that tears up the deal still leaves SanDisk capturing ~25%, so a -50% market price translates to an effective ASP of only ~-25%. In practice 'tearing up' = renegotiating for more years at a lower price. All high-capacity drives (128/256TB) are QLC, where SanDisk + Kioxia 'have done very well.'

JPM corroborates the LTA layer at TMC: SanDisk extended the undersupply call from end-CY26 to end-CY27; the three signed LTAs carry floor-and-ceiling pricing and pre-pay-style walkaways with financial guarantees; BiCS 8 (200L+, TLC+QLC) executing well.
GS went into 'full bullish mode' on memory stocks, citing MU + SNDK.
MS (OW) raised PT to $1,750 (from $1,100), up +59%; SNDK repeatedly cited in GOOG's $80B AI supply-chain map for NAND (ParadisLabs).

MS rates NAND fundamentals '8 of 10' vs DRAM '10/10'; SanDisk has become 'everyone's preferred investment' and is the price-setter ('being the bad guy,' Koreans pricing just below), but MS still prefers Micron because SanDisk looks more expensive on 2028 numbers. Some 2028 LTA lock-in prices are down vs 2027 ('materially' in some cases, esp. enterprise TLC). Q3 NAND pricing seen +20-30% QoQ.

Conor prefers Kioxia over SanDisk on the latency angle for agentic AI: SanDisk's HPF (its answer to Kioxia's Super IO/XL Flash, in design with Global Unichip) only ships in 2028, by which point Super IO SLC will have been shipping for ~2 years. Direct read: 'if Super IO works, HPF is dead on arrival.'

The sharpest NAND pricing datapoint of the quarter, and it is a reversal of the analyst's own view from a month earlier. Moore had described the market as "wobbly a little bit… Some of the LTAs were seeing some pushback. Q3 price negotiations were tough." Now: "I'm not sure what's happened, but in the last 30 days that's completely changed. Like the NAND market has strengthened materially. I'm seeing prices now above 70 cents, multiple transactions, which would be up 60, 70% from Q2. In enterprise the NAND market has become very, very strong." Three reasons it matters here: transacted enterprise NAND above 70 cents is a harder datapoint than a contract-price forecast and runs ahead of the published forecasts on the page (BofA +35% q/q F4Q26 ASP, 07-01; UBS +30% q/q 3Q26 contract, 07-03); the LTA pushback that was the live threat to the NBM durability narrative has reversed; and it is explicitly enterprise-only — "not talking about PCs and phones" — with the weakness confined to consumer/PC/smartphone NAND. Positioning caveat kept alongside it: SNDK ranks FOURTH in Moore's own coverage, "Nvidia, Broadcom, then Micron, then Sandisk… there's nothing else that's wildly compelling" — bullish the NAND tape, last of four on the stock.

cells: Bits flat y/y; growth is price/mix
